mathematical_review.literal_formula: The rational polynomial contains exactly i=0..n, divided by i!. The remainder is abs(q)^(n+1)/(n+1)!, matching the inspected actual Mathlib Lagrange theorem, not its distinct Cauchy remainder. Rational-to-real casts and q=0 are supplied internally.
mathematical_review.derivative_domain: Real.iter_deriv_exp identifies every iterated derivative with exp. The entire closed unordered segment from 0 to q<=0 lies in the nonpositive half-line, so the derivative bound is one including both endpoints. Author uses the Lagrange interior point; an independent parametric kernel discriminator proves the stronger closed-segment fact.
mathematical_review.clipping: q<=-T, including equality, returns [0,2^-T]. exp(1)>=2, exp natural multiples and inverse monotonicity prove the upper bound. exp positivity proves the zero lower bound. This is a sound enclosure, not a statement that the tail amplitude or mass is zero. Active q has abs(q)<T. Huge input only selects the clipped branch; no Taylor power on that branch is evaluated.
mathematical_review.width: checked requires q<=0, positive epsilon and actual full interval width<=epsilon. Tail width remains 2^-T and active width is 2*radius. Independent exact fixtures reject a clipped interval wider than epsilon and refuse positive q/zero epsilon. Author also refuses negative epsilon and insufficient active degree.
mathematical_review.allocation: tailCutoff is the actual rational-ceiling/max/clog producer. Its tail width theorem and threshold-size theorem are ordinary kernel proofs. No active-degree completeness, input-size translation or runtime guarantee follows.
mathematical_review.actual_consumers: Complete original HermitePolynomial source was read. hermite_left uses smoothInitial=exp(p) at p<-1; hermite_right uses exp(-p) at p>0; endpoint_scalar uses exp(-1). These are actual signed function-value semantics at rational coordinates. They do not identify the original irrational piL grid with stored rational coordinates or certify the middle polynomial path.
mathematical_review.global_boundary: Scalar epsilon is enclosure width only. No dimension aggregation, normalization or other pipeline stage is supplied by this package. Clipping cannot be read as silently discarded mass or renormalized-away error.
mathematical_review.huge_input: checked(-10^1000,2^-80,80,0) reproduced as an interpreter output only. The actual concrete kernel exp(-80) bound is distinct. No huge-input kernel theorem is claimed.
